title: Drone Sim
description: Autonomous quadcopter that flies itself through a city in the browser, with a C++ flight core compiled to WebAssembly.
stat: 1000 of 1000 test flights reached the goal, in calm air and in wind

media.alt: A quadcopter flying over a city intersection, with the lidar points it sees and its planned path drawn in

details:
Drone Sim is an autonomous quadcopter in the browser. The C++ core (6 DOF physics, a cascaded PID controller, 3D A*, a Kalman filter and a simulated lidar) runs as WebAssembly in a three.js city with a physical sky, soft shadows and glass that reflects it.

What you can do

- Pick a waypoint route, a lawnmower search or go home, where it climbs, flies back and lands on the pad
- Tap to set goals, drop boxes in its way and add wind, and watch it replan

Results

- Over 1000 seeded cities it reached the goal on 1000 of 1000 flights in calm air and 1000 of 1000 in wind
- Over 100 cities its search covered at least 99.78% of the area in calm air

title: ResumeFit
description: Free resume match and job application assistant.
stat: About 6,860 skills matched · 30+ checks · 480 unit and 33 browser tests
details:
ResumeFit is a free web app and Chrome extension that scores a resume against a job description, shows what is missing, and keeps every application in one tracker. I wanted a resume scanner for me and my friends with no paywalls, credits or locked features, and a score I could explain.

What I built

- A scoring engine in plain code: hard skills 50%, soft skills 15%, searchability 15%, recruiter tips 10%, formatting 10%
- PDF and DOCX readers that rebuild lines from text positions and document XML, so fonts, columns, tables and margins can be checked
- A Manifest V3 Chrome extension that scans the job posting on the page you are on and fills in application forms from a saved profile
- A drag and drop application tracker, and a resume builder with 8 templates and PDF and Word export
- Writing help that tries Gemini, then Groq, then Cloudflare Workers AI, on free tiers only

Results

- About 6,860 skills matched per scan, 6,559 of them imported from the O*NET database and the rest picked by hand
- 30+ report checks and 11 applicant tracking systems detected
- 480 unit and data layer tests, 33 browser tests, and accessibility checks on 16 pages
- 17 database tables, with row level security on every one

Limits

My first auto apply feature did not hold up on real company sites, so I removed about 4,800 lines and rebuilt it smaller. The new one has been tested against saved copies of real forms, not yet on live applications. Sign in is invite only by default, and there is no usage data or feedback from other people yet.

title: Event Horizon
description: A real-time black hole you can fly around and spin up in the browser, with every pixel a light ray traced through curved space.
stat: Matches general relativity to 1 part in 100,000
details: Event Horizon is a real-time black hole you can fly around in the browser. Every pixel is a light ray traced through curved space in a WebGL2 shader, checked pixel by pixel against a C++ reference tracer that matches general relativity to 1 part in 100,000. A spin slider turns it into a spinning (Kerr) black hole, and a bloom pass gives the glowing disk a film look.

media.alt: A black hole with its glowing disk bent into an arch over the top by gravity

title: Gravity Sandbox
description: N-body gravity in the browser, written in C++ and compiled to WebAssembly.
stat: SIMD 2.44x faster · 3.26x on 4 threads · 44 physics tests
details:
Watch two galaxies collide, a black hole shred a star cluster, or three bodies chase each other round a figure eight. A C++17 core with a Barnes-Hut octree does the physics, three.js draws it straight from WebAssembly memory, and a React panel changes speed, accuracy and star count. Click to drop in a new body, and a live readout shows how well energy holds while it runs.

Results

- WebAssembly SIMD makes brute force 2.44x faster
- The tree walk is split across threads, 3.26x faster on 4 threads for a 10,000 star disk
- 44 tests check the physics

media.alt: Two galaxies of glowing stars drifting toward each other in the dark

title: TinyGPT
description: A GPT-style language model built from scratch that runs in your browser.
stat: 27.4M parameters · about 329M training tokens · about 75 tokens/sec on WebGPU
details:
TinyGPT is a small language model I wrote myself instead of using a library: my own tokenizer, my own transformer and my own training loop. I trained it on recipes, so you type the name of a dish and it writes the ingredients and steps. I built it to understand how GPT-style models work by writing every piece, and so anyone can try one in a click with no server behind it.

What I built

- A byte-level BPE tokenizer with a 4,096 token vocabulary, in Python and again in TypeScript, checked against 20 shared test inputs
- A decoder-only transformer with hand-written multi-head attention
- A training loop with AdamW, warmup then cosine decay, mixed precision, and checkpoints that resume bit-for-bit
- An ONNX export that runs in the browser on WebGPU, with a WebAssembly fallback on the CPU
- Views of the tokens, the top 10 guesses at every step, and what each attention head was looking at

Results

- 27.4M parameter model trained on about 329M tokens of recipes: 36,000 steps in 2 h 59 min on one RTX 3060, validation loss 1.430
- About 75 tokens/sec on WebGPU in Chrome
- A smaller 10.5M parameter model reached validation loss 1.537 in 48 min

Limits

The model has learned which words tend to follow which. It does not have a real idea of cooking, so ingredients listed at the top don't always get used. Safari has not been tested.

title: Bird Identifier
description: Fine-tuned ConvNeXt-V2 model that classifies 555 North American bird species.
details:
Bird Identifier names 555 North American bird species from one photo. You upload a picture and get the most likely species with a confidence score, the other top possibilities, a Wikipedia summary and the species' conservation status. I do computer vision work at my internship and shoot wildlife photos myself, so I wanted an end-to-end vision project of my own.

What I built

- A ConvNeXt-V2-Base model (about 88.3M parameters) fine-tuned on the NABirds dataset with Mixup, CutMix, label smoothing and EMA
- Evaluation with temperature scaling for calibration and Grad-CAM overlays to see what the model looks at
- A FastAPI service that runs on ONNX Runtime with no PyTorch, with upload limits and rate limiting
- A React front end that resizes photos in the browser and pulls species info from Wikipedia and Wikidata
- A Docker image on Render for the API, and Vercel for the front end

Results

- 89.00% top-1 and 98.78% top-5 accuracy on 24,633 test images
- Trained on 21,519 images in about 3.3 hours on one RTX 3060
- Expected calibration error went from 0.134 to 0.037 after temperature scaling
- ONNX fp32 runs at 145 ms p50 on the CPU, against 198 ms for PyTorch
- 62 automated tests

Limits

The free host only fits the 85.6 MB INT8 model, which is slower than fp32, and the first request after idle takes 30 to 60 seconds. Rare classes are weak: some have only 3 to 9 training images.

title: Stock Movement Predictor
description: ML pipeline that predicts S&P 500 stock movement, served through a Flask API.
details:
You pick a stock ticker and the app predicts whether it goes up or down over the next day, week or month, with a confidence level, a plain-language verdict and a price chart. I built it to do machine learning on a problem where it is very easy to fool yourself, with a method I can defend end to end. The honest result is that no model beats the baseline.

What I built

- A pipeline over daily prices for 499 S&P 500 companies from January 2016 to June 2026, with 24 features that only use information available at or before prediction time
- Logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting models for three horizons, compared against naive baselines on a chronological holdout
- A Flask API that fetches recent data live and returns the direction, a confidence level and a verdict
- Accounts and a watchlist with scrypt-hashed passwords, and a React front end, shipped as one Docker image on Render

Results

- About 1.27 million rows after feature engineering: 1,011,331 for training and 260,960 for testing on the next-day horizon
- Next-day test accuracy of 0.520, the same as the majority baseline. Next week 0.531 against 0.534, next month 0.553 against 0.554
- A leakage bug made cross-validation show 65.7% for a model that scored 50.8% on the holdout. Fixed, it was about 52%
- 46 automated tests

Limits

The model does not predict market direction better than chance from daily price data, and the app says so. This is an educational demo, not investment advice.
